en: The Section on the Training Rules (Sekhiyakaṇḍa)
The Training Rule on Being Well-Restrained.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the group-of-six monks were walking through inhabited areas playing with their hands and feet... [etc. ...
"The training is to be observed: 'I shall walk well-restrained in inhabited areas.
One should walk in inhabited areas being well-restrained."
If one, out of disrespect, walks through an inhabited area playing with one's hand or foot, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
There is no offense if it was unintentional.
In the case of one who is absent-minded, one who is unaware, or one who is ill.
"In the case of one who is insane,
or in the case of the first offender.
The fifth training rule is concluded.
